s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual field defect with worsening headaches and history of intracerebral hemorrhage
salient_findings: Left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage on noncontrast head CT
Left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage on contrast-enhanced brain MRI
key_facts: 36-year-old Asian man
4-month history of worsening headaches
Complete right homonymous hemianopia
History of left occipital intracerebral hematoma of unknown cause 2 years earlier
Normal vital signs
Neurologic testing confirmed visual field defect without other focal deficits
Left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage on noncontrast head CT
Left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage on contrast-enhanced brain MRI
Subtotal removal of mass during left occipital craniotomy
Mass invaded falx cerebri and adjacent cortex
Histopathological examination showed spindle cells with branching ectatic vasculature and up to 20 mitoses per ten high-power fields

differentials: Malignant fibrous histiocytoma of the meninges
per_call: Malignant fibrous histiocytoma of the meninges

shortlist.label: Hemangiopericytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination showed spindle cells with branching ectatic vasculature and strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1, consistent with hemangiopericytoma

shortlist.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Similar histopathological features to hemangiopericytoma, but less likely given the presence of up to 20 mitoses per ten high-power fields

shortlist.label: Anaplastic hemangiopericytoma
shortlist.why_kept: High mitotic rate and invasive growth pattern suggest a more aggressive variant of hemangiopericytoma

shortlist.label: Malignant solitary fibrous tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to anaplastic hemangiopericytoma, but less likely given the specific immunohistochemical profile

shortlist.label: Cavernous angioma
shortlist.why_kept: Initial diagnosis based on imaging findings, but histopathological examination revealed a more complex lesion

raw.rationale: The histopathological examination showing spindle cells with branching ectatic vasculature and strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1 supports the diagnosis of Hemangiopericytoma.

rejected.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
rejected.why: Lack of strong immunoreactivity for CD34 and Bcl-2, which are typically positive in solitary fibrous tumors

rejected.label: Anaplastic hemangiopericytoma
rejected.why: Although the tumor has a high mitotic rate, the presence of up to 20 mitoses per ten high-power fields alone is not sufficient to classify it as anaplastic without other high-grade features

rejected.label: Malignant solitary fibrous tumor
rejected.why: Similar reasoning as for solitary fibrous tumor, with additional consideration of the tumor's morphology and immunophenotype not aligning with malignant solitary fibrous tumor

rejected.label: Cavernous angioma
rejected.why: The initial suspicion based on imaging was not supported by histopathological findings, which did not show the characteristic features of a cavernous angioma
